f.title: Submit the SAE reporting form to be used in the study with the application
f.statement: The clinical trial application must include blank case report forms and the serious adverse events reporting form to be used in the study.

rows.quote:
1.4.13 Blank Case Report Forms (CRFs) and Serious Adverse Events reporting form to be
used in the study.
rows.review_note: Review: list item under the application contents (1.4); obligation follows from the requirement to submit a complete application. Double-check: modal implicit; below 90.

f.title: Provide an updated risk-benefit assessment and consequences for participants with amendment applications
f.statement: The applicant must submit supporting data for an amendment, as far as possible including an updated overall risk-benefit assessment, possible consequences for participants already in the trial, possible consequences for the assessment of trial results, and summaries of data.

rows.quote:
1.11.4 The applicant must also submit supporting data for the amendment, including as
possible;
a. Updated overall risk-benefit assessment
b. Possible consequences for participants already in the trial
rows.review_note: Review: must = Mandatory; limited to safety-relevant items. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Obtain TMDA approval before amendments affecting safety, monitoring or drug quality
f.statement: TMDA approval must be obtained for amendments including changes that affect patient selection and monitoring, clinical efficacy and safety requirements (e.g. dosage adjustments, study procedures), patient discontinuation, and chemistry and manufacturing information that may affect drug safety and quality.

rows.quote:
1.11.5 TMDA approval must be obtained for the following amendments:
(i) Changes that affect patient selection and monitoring
(ii) Changes that affect clinical efficacy and safety requirements (e.g. dosage
adjustments, study procedures, etc)
(iii) Changes that affect patient discontinuation
rows.review_note: Review: only the safety-related categories are curated; item (vii) (CMC changes affecting safety and quality) is cited in the statement from the same list. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Establish a DSMB/DMC where safety concerns are unusually high
f.statement: A data safety monitoring board or committee shall be established to enhance the safety of trial participants where safety concerns may be unusually high; DMCs are generally recommended for any controlled trial comparing rates of mortality or major morbidity. A DSMB/DMC shall be considered e.g. where interim results may require early termination, there are a priori safety concerns, prior information suggests serious toxicity, the population is fragile or vulnerable, the population is at elevated risk of death or serious outcomes, or the study is large, long and multi-centre.
f.clause: 1.13.9 Requirements concerning DSMB/DMC (numbered 1.1.9.1 in the text)

rows.quote:
1.1.9.1 The clinical trial shall be required to establish a data safety monitoring board or
committee to enhance the safety of trial participants in situations in which safety
concerns may be unusually high. DMCs are generally recommended for any
controlled trial of any size that will compare rates of mortality or major morbidity.
The DSMB/DMC shall be considered in the following situations;
rows.location: 1.13.9 Requirements concerning DSMB/DMC (numbered 1.1.9.1 in the text)
rows.review_note: Review: section numbering in the captured text is inconsistent (1.1.9.x under heading 1.13.9). Mandatory for high-concern trials, recommended for mortality/morbidity comparisons; level follows the headline 'shall'. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Appoint DSMB/DMC members with relevant expertise, no serious conflicts and one local expert
f.statement: The sponsor shall appoint DSMB/DMC members with relevant expertise, experience in clinical trials and on other DMCs, and absence of serious conflicts of interest; at least one member should be a local expert.

rows.quote:
1.1.9.2 The sponsor shall appoint members of a DSMB/DMC by considering selection of
individuals with relevant expertise, experience in clinical trials and in serving on
other DMCs, and absence of serious conflicts of interest.
rows.review_note: Review: the local-member element ('should') is in the following sentence of the same paragraph and the charter list (e). Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit a DSMB/DMC charter with the prescribed content
f.statement: The applicant shall submit a DSMB/DMC charter covering aims and objectives, terms of reference, composition, member qualifications, one local member, roles including statisticians, statistical stopping rules, relationship with investigators and trial management, decision-making powers, meeting organisation, blinding, options it can recommend, form and recipients of decisions, reporting line, role in publication, and disclosure of competing interests.

rows.quote:
1.1.9.3 The applicants shall submit a DSMB/DMC charter with following details:
(a) A broad statement of the aims and objectives of the DSMB/DMC
rows.review_note: Review: list items (b)-(p) summarised in the statement from the same list. Double-check: statement lists items outside the short quote; 86.

f.title: Sponsor may appoint an Independent Safety Monitor for low-risk small phase I/II trials
f.statement: For low-risk smaller phase I or II trials that do not require a full DSMB or DMC, the sponsor may appoint an Independent Safety Monitor (ISM), a physician with expertise in the relevant study area who reviews all adverse events occurring in the study.
f.applicability: Low-risk smaller phase I or II trials

rows.quote:
1.13.9.4 The Sponsor may appoint an Independent Safety Monitor (ISM) for low risk
smaller phase I or II trials that do not require a full DSMB or DMC. The ISM shall
be a physician with an expertise in the relevant study area who will be reviewing
all adverse events that may occur from the study.

f.title: Report fatal or life-threatening SAEs/SUSARs to TMDA within 24 hours
f.statement: All serious adverse events, including SUSARs, that are fatal or life-threatening should be reported to TMDA within 24 hours by telephone, fax or e-mail.
f.applicability: Fatal or life-threatening SAEs and SUSARs in trials in Tanzania

rows.quote:
1.14.3.1 All serious adverse events (SAEs) including suspected unexpected serious
adverse reactions (SUSARs) that are fatal or life-threatening should be reported to
TMDA within 24 hours by telephone, facsimile transmission, or e-mail followed by
a complete report within 7 additional calendar days of their occurrence.
rows.review_note: Review: 'should' = Recommended per the source modal, although the TZ CT Regulations 2013 (reg 19) make SUSAR reporting mandatory within 7 days. Clock: the text ties the timelines to 'their occurrence'; the 24-hour clock start is not stated separately, so clock_start uses that wording. Double-check: modal and clock start uncertain; below 90.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Fatal or life-threatening SAEs/SUSARs - initial notification

f.title: Submit a complete report on fatal or life-threatening SAEs/SUSARs within 7 additional days
f.statement: The initial 24-hour notification of a fatal or life-threatening SAE/SUSAR should be followed by a complete report within 7 additional calendar days; the report must include an assessment of the importance and implications of the findings, including relevant previous experience with the same or similar medicinal products.
f.applicability: Fatal or life-threatening SAEs and SUSARs
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Submission operations; Medical review

rows.deadline: Complete report within 7 additional calendar days
rows.quote:
followed by
a complete report within 7 additional calendar days of their occurrence. The report
must include an assessment of the importance and implication of the findings,
including relevant previous experience with the same or similar medicinal products.
rows.review_note: Review: timing 'should' (Recommended); content 'must' (Mandatory) - row level follows the timing headline. The 7 days are 'additional' to the initial notification while also tied to 'occurrence'; ambiguous. Double-check: below 90.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Fatal or life-threatening SAEs/SUSARs - complete report (after the 24-hour notification)

f.title: Report other SAEs and SUSARs within 14 calendar days of first knowledge by the sponsor
f.statement: All other SAEs and SUSARs that are not fatal or life-threatening must be filed as soon as possible but no later than 14 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor.
f.applicability: SAEs and SUSARs that are not fatal or life-threatening

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 14 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor
rows.quote:
1.14.3.2 All other SAEs and SUSARs that are not fatal or life-threatening must be filed
as soon as possible but no later than 14 calendar days after first knowledge by the
sponsor.

deadline_rule.clock_start:
after first knowledge by the
sponsor

f.title: Use a trial-specific or the Annex 15 SAE form with trial identifiers
f.statement: The applicant should develop a trial-specific form or use the Annex 15 reporting form, followed by detailed written reports; when completing the CIOMS form, trial-specific details such as participant ID numbers and/or protocol number should be included.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote:
1.14.3.3 The applicant should develop a trial specific form or use the reporting form
attached as Annex 15 followed by detailed written reports. When completing the
CIOMS form, trial specific details such as the participants ID numbers and/or
protocol number should be included.

f.title: Report protocol-specified critical AEs and laboratory abnormalities
f.statement: Adverse events and/or laboratory abnormalities identified in the protocol as critical to safety evaluations should also be reported.

rows.quote:
1.14.3.4 Adverse events and/or laboratory abnormalities identified in the protocol as
critical to safety evaluations should also be reported.

f.title: Submit additional information such as autopsy reports for reported deaths
f.statement: For reported deaths, additional information (e.g. autopsy reports and terminal medical reports) should be submitted.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote:
1.14.3.5 For reported deaths, additional information (e.g., autopsy reports and terminal
medical reports) should be submitted.

f.title: Establish, evaluate and submit the relationship between each SAE/SUSAR and the IMP
f.statement: The relationship between SAE(s)/SUSARs and the investigational medicinal product must be established, evaluated, clarified and submitted to TMDA for further assessment.
f.clause: 1.14.3 Reporting of SAEs/SUSARs (numbered 1.15.3.6 in the text)

rows.quote:
1.15.3.6 The relationship between SAE(s)/SUSARs and the IMP must be established,
evaluated, clarified and submitted to TMDA for further assessment.
rows.location: 1.14.3 Reporting of SAEs/SUSARs (numbered 1.15.3.6 in the text)

f.title: Expedited reporting applies to investigational, comparator and BA/BE study products
f.statement: The expedited reporting applies to clinical trials of investigational products, comparator products and products used in bioavailability (BA) and bioequivalence (BE) studies.
f.applicability: Investigational products, comparators, BA/BE study products

rows.quote:
1.14.3.6 The expedited reporting is applicable for clinical trials of investigational
products, comparator products and for products used in bioavailability (BA) and
bioequivalence (BE) studies.
rows.review_note: Review: scope statement that widens what must be reported (comparators, BA/BE); recorded as Mandatory as it defines the reach of 1.14.3.2. Double-check: descriptive wording; 88.

f.title: On premature termination, inform TMDA within 15 days and advise investigators of risks to participants
f.statement: If a clinical trial is terminated by the principal investigator or sponsor in its entirety, TMDA must be informed not later than 15 days after the date of termination, with the reasons and impact; all co-investigators must be informed as soon as possible and advised in writing of potential risks to the health of participants or other persons, including ensuring that patients continue to receive medical care.

rows.deadline: Not later than 15 days after the date of termination
rows.quote:
If a clinical trial is terminated by the principal investigator or sponsor in its entirety, the
principal investigator or sponsor must inform TMDA not later than 15 days after the date
of the termination; and must:
rows.review_note: Review: the safety element (1.16.1.2 advise of potential risks, continued medical care) is summarised from the list that follows the quote. Days read as calendar days. Double-check: below 90 as the statement extends beyond the quote.

deadline_rule.clock_start:
after the date
of the termination
deadline_rule.applies_to: Notification of premature termination of a trial

f.title: Report any unexpected safety issue changing the risk-benefit at trial close with proposed actions
f.statement: At the end of the trial, any unexpected safety issue that changes the risk-benefit analysis and is likely to have an impact on trial participants should be reported together with proposed actions to be taken.
f.topic: Safety issues at end of trial

rows.quote:
1.16.3.2 Any unexpected safety issue that changes the risks-benefit analysis and is
likely to have an impact on trial participants should be reported together with
proposed actions to be taken.

f.title: Describe safety assessment and AE reporting procedures in the protocol
f.statement: The study protocol should include the assessment of safety: specification of safety parameters; methods and timing for assessing, recording and analysing safety parameters; procedures for eliciting, recording and reporting adverse events and intercurrent illnesses; and the type and duration of follow-up of subjects after adverse events.
f.clause: Annex 3 Contents of study protocol, 3.8 Assessment of safety

rows.quote:
3.8.2 The methods and timing for assessing, recording, and analyzing safety
parameters.
3.8.3 Procedures for eliciting reports of and for recording and reporting adverse
events and intercurrent illnesses.
rows.location: Annex 3 Contents of study protocol, 3.8 Assessment of safety
rows.review_note: Review: annex content list; modal implicit, recorded as Recommended. 3.8.1 and 3.8.4 cited in the statement. Double-check: 85.
